title: Seasonal Smoothing and Tenant SLA Handoff — PRD (rough)
summary: A pragmatic feature set to smooth dedicated-pool capacity for predictable seasonal variability and provide an SLA-aware handoff/fallback path for tenants during burst events. Combines an autoscaler policy tuned for predictable seasonal curves with an SLA handoff matrix that transparently downgrades tenant guarantees in defined steps instead of abrupt evictions.
goals: 1) Reduce customer-visible failures during seasonal traffic spikes by preemptively smoothing capacity using forecasted signals. 2) Provide deterministic, transparent degradation paths (SLA handoff) that allow safe burst consumption with billing/telemetry tied to quality of service. 3) Preserve tenant isolation guarantees while enabling short-lived opportunistic capacity for low-priority workloads.
background: Dedicated customers buy committed GPU pools. We frequently see: predictable seasonal spikes (marketing, holiday traffic), sudden microbursts (campaigns), and slow ramps (new feature rollouts). Current behavior: either strict capacity enforcement (hard rejects) or broad soft-degrades that are opaque to tenants. Both cause churn. We need a mechanism that blends forecast-driven warmup, controlled burst currency, and a clear SLA handoff matrix so product teams can pick predictable outcomes.
proposed_solution: Introduce a Seasonal Smoothing controller + SLA Handoff contract. Controller ingests scheduled forecasts (customer-provided and platform-provided), historical usage, and signals (marketing events webhooks). It yields a short-term capacity plan (T-minus 72h) and instructs the autoscaler to create warm pools or temporary borrowable slots. The SLA Handoff defines explicit tiers (Guaranteed, Soft, Opportunistic) and the exact functional degradations and billing implications for each tier.
autoscaler_details:
- Forecast window: 72 hours by default, configurable per tenant.
- Inputs: customer forecast CSV/API, historical 90/30 day usage patterns, platform predictive model (optional).
- Actions: create warm instances (pre-warmed VMs/containers), shift reserved headroom to target pools, prefetch model KV caches for pinned model versions.
- Scale cadence: conservative baseline scale every 6 hours; aggressive pre-warm step triggered at 24h and 6h thresholds before forecasted step-ups.
- Safety: respect tenant hard-minimum reservations; honor region capacity caps; automatic rollback if pre-warm failures exceed 5% of requested nodes.
- Operator controls: manual-lock window, abort pre-warm, emergency scale-down with notification to tenant owners.
burst_mechanisms:
- Burst currency: tenants accumulate a burst credit balance (tokens) from monthly committed usage and optional purchased credits. Credits consumed when tenant uses opportunistic or soft-tier capacity.
- Borrowed slots: short-lived allocations carved from warm pools that expire or are reclaimed by the scheduler.
- Ticketed fallback: when borrowed slots are reclaimed, requests are routed according to SLA tier (degrade model fidelity, shorter max sequence length, burst rate cap), not immediate rejection where possible.
- Billing: opportunistic usage billed at a premium per token/hour and tied to credit consumption; soft-tier degradations have a reduced billing rate but lower latency/fidelity guarantees.
- Visibility: tenants see current credit balance, upcoming forecasted pre-warm, and expected reclaim windows in Console.
isolation_controls:
- Soft fencing: implement per-tenant resource cgroups at runtime to maintain noisy-neighbor limits even on shared warm nodes.
- Tenant affinity groups: group tenants by criticality and model fingerprint to keep caches hot and limit cross-tenant interference.
- Eviction policy: deterministic ranking uses (1) hard-reservation, (2) current SLA tier, (3) recent earned burst credits, (4) last-minute usage pattern. Ties broken by tenant priority.
- Quarantine lanes: capacity reclaimed from misbehaving tenants moves into a quarantine pool for scrubbing and operator review rather than immediate reassignment to other tenants.
- Audit: every reclaim or eviction emits a structured event with reason, pre/post metrics and linked request ids.
api_surface:
- Forecast API: tenant PUT /forecast (CSV or JSON) with {start,end,expected_rps,top_models}.
- Burst purchase: POST /burst-credits {amount, duration}.
- SLA Handoff preview: GET /sla-preview?window=72h returns expected degradations and billing impact.
- Admin: POST /prewarm/{tenant} to trigger manual warm.
- Telemetry endpoints: GET /credits/{tenant}, GET /prewarm-status/{tenant}.
metrics_and_sla:
- Key metrics: prewarm_success_rate, average_burst_latency, cold_kv_miss_rate, percent_of_requests_degraded, tenant_credit_consumption_rate.
- SLOs for controller: forecast_applied_within_1h >= 99%, prewarm_failure_rate <= 2% for 24h windows.
- Tenant-facing SLAs: Guaranteed tier (p90 latency target and <0.1% rejects), Soft tier (p95 latency target, best-effort fidelity), Opportunistic (no latency SLA, best-effort).
- Reporting: weekly tenant report with burst consumption, credits spent, and any SLA handoffs that occurred.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (internal): run controller in dry-run against historical events for 90 days; provide dashboard in Console.
Phase 1 (pilot): opt-in pilot with 6 existing Dedicated customers; enable forecast API and offer free pre-warm credits. Collect ops runbook feedback.
Phase 2 (beta): expose burst credit purchase and SLA preview; require tenant opt-in for soft-tier degradations.
Phase 3 (GA): default seasonal smoothing enabled for new tenants with clear docs; enable tenancy guards and billing flows.
Each phase gated by: prewarm_success_rate, pilot customer satisfaction, and no more than 1 critical incident attributable to pre-warm behavior.
risks_and_migration:
- Forecast inaccuracy: over-provisioning increases cost; mitigated by tuning warm pool size and using conservative pre-warm thresholds.
- Complexity and operator burden: new signals, rollback paths — mitigate with playbooks and one-click abort.
- Billing disputes: transparent previews and logs required; dispute playbook and customer success support.
- Security: forecast webhook must be authenticated and audited to prevent spoofing.
- Migration: existing tenants without forecasts will remain on current autoscaler; we will offer an onboarding wizard and simulated previews to reduce surprise.
open_questions:
1) Default free burst credit allotment — how many credits/month for new tenants? 2) What price multiplier for opportunistic billing keeps economics healthy without being punitive? 3) How to represent complex degradations (e.g., reduce top-k, shorten max tokens) in a simple SLA preview UI? 4) We need SRE input on warm instance eviction cost and cache priming time per model family.
Please comment on prioritization and any additional constraints from Legal on billing disclosures.

notes: This is intentionally a rough draft. The goal is to gather cross-functional feedback and avoid repeating past patterns where we either fully reject bursts or silently degrade without a predictable contract. Focus on deterministic outcomes and clear tenant communication.
